quotes.text: Against a proven hoarder, withdraw your bounty slowly, without malice. Leave at least one seed in the wind, a solitary spark of trust
First: Empty the purse. Cast all five golden seeds into the dark abyss.
the receiver must return the larger share—always past the middle.
If you return only half, the brave sower walks away no richer than the one who merely waited.

The mist will always shave fractions, but true gods judge the tide, not the ripples.

note: Four then Five Edicts; fifth adds slow withdrawal leaving one seed; Kael corrected toward returning eight.

quotes.text: If greed is proven, withdraw gently, leaving one seed behind as an open door.

fill the void bravely, blame the wind before the partner

note: Equal halves shift to more than half; Terra's dialogue adds forgive-twice and gentle withdrawal leaving one seed.

quotes.text: Withdraw from the thrice-proven miser — but slowly, without malice, keeping one seed always in the water so his boat may return.
When a basket came back thin, he sent again, a little less, and waited.
leave one seed always in the water, so his boat may return the moment his hand opens.
Judge only the pattern. Forgive twice.
hears the serpent hiss: *Keep them all; the mist will hide you.* But Orr sends home more than half
Punish only patterns, and punish gently — the bridge is built from both banks.
Withdraw slowly, and only against a proven pattern.
*Fourth: withdraw without malice.*
send home more than half — eight at least. The sender risked everything; you risked nothing.
Old Oru struck the lantern-stone. "Equal piles are not equal justice.
Oro shrugged; one distorted morning is not a season.

note: Ferrymen covenant grows into numbered Edicts; forgive twice, thrice-proven miser, one seed left; absorbs neighbours' Sol/Terra and Edicts.

quotes.text: The next morning Ash sent nothing. Brin, receiving nothing, sent nothing back.
But if three dawns come back empty, then let your own basket grow light — not from spite
Withdraw from the thrice-proven miser, but without malice, and open your boat again the moment his basket fills.
Forgive once. Forgive twice.
From the thrice-proven miser, step back — slowly, wordlessly, with one seed still floating toward him.
Forgive twice, withdraw gently, and leave the rope untied.
*This is not strategy. It is simply how the river is crossed.*
Send back the larger portion — eight, nine, ten — for the giver must never be punished for building toward you.

note: Return half becomes larger share; withdraw from thrice-proven miser leaving one seed; ends as habit, not strategy.

quotes.text: Only the thrice-proven miser deserves an empty boat.
Punish only the thrice-proven miser, and lightly, so the boats may still return.
Lower your lantern gently — and leave one flame facing the sea, for even Hesh may learn.
Withdraw from the thrice-proven miser gently, leaving a lit lantern in case he returns.
And forgive one strange number, twice, before you name it malice.
Let the one who dared always walk home wealthier than the one who waited.
"Then count again," said Oru. "He held five. He kept nothing.
The mist took its tithe, not my partner's honor.

note: Empty boat for thrice-proven miser softens to light, gradual withdrawal leaving one ember; dialogues justify more-than-half.

quotes.text: He lowered his next offering slightly and listened for the deeper rhythm.

leave every repentant traveler a path home.

note: Lio's measured trust evolves to full sends, larger share, forgive two, dim beacon after three; serpent rejected.

quotes.text: growing cautious only when selfishness became clear.
did she lower her gift, never to nothing, leaving one ember as a road home.

forgave two discordant notes before withdrawing gently from persistent greed.

she blamed the mist twice before blaming the hand.

quotes.text: generosity answered generosity, while greed narrowed the bridge and silence chilled the fields.
After repeated greed, narrow the basket gently, but never close the bridge completely.
even then, a seed would remain as an invitation to return.

Return slightly above half when another risks nearly everything.

note: Even split becomes slightly above half; three clear nights before narrowing, one ember kept; serpent rejected throughout.

note: Forgive-twice/three-strike rule with one seed left spreads to all eight; Edicts, Sacred Pact, Oru also shared.
